patches.old: In contrast, neurological amnesias (e.g., from hippocampal damage in Korsakoff syndrome) typically show severe anterograde amnesia with relatively preserved remote memories.
patches.new: In contrast, neurological amnesias typically show severe anterograde amnesia with relatively preserved remote memories. Two classic examples: bilateral medial temporal lobe damage, as in the patient H.M., and **Korsakoff syndrome**, which follows thiamine deficiency and damages the **mammillary bodies and the medial thalamic nuclei** rather than the hippocampus itself. Both produce the opposite profile from dissociative amnesia: new learning fails, while identity and remote autobiographical memory are largely intact.

patches.old: ASPD is significantly more common in males than females (approximately 3:1 ratio) and is highly prevalent in incarcerated populations (estimated 50–80% of prisoners meet criteria).
patches.new: ASPD is significantly more common in males than females (approximately 3:1 ratio) and is heavily over-represented in incarcerated populations. The largest systematic review of prison surveys found that about **47% of male prisoners and about 21% of female prisoners** met criteria for ASPD, with roughly two-thirds of male prisoners meeting criteria for some personality disorder. Be wary of the higher figures sometimes quoted; they come from selected forensic samples rather than general prison populations.

sources.title: Fazel & Danesh, “Serious mental disorder in 23000 prisoners: a systematic review of 62 surveys”, Lancet (2002) — 47% of male and 21% of female prisoners met criteria for antisocial personality disorder

visual.title: The clusters, the syntony question, and the dissociation continuum
visual.alt: Three columns listing the odd, dramatic and anxious clusters with the signature feature of each of the ten personality disorders; a panel contrasting ego-syntonic traits, which feel like part of the self and bring the person in only when someone else insists, with ego-dystonic symptoms, which feel alien and drive help-seeking; and a continuum from daydreaming through depersonalization and derealization and dissociative amnesia with fugue to dissociative identity disorder.
visual.caption: Ask whether the trait feels right to the person before reaching for a diagnosis — it separates the personality disorders from everything else, and OCPD from OCD.
